data.one_liner: Performant hierarchical state machine framework inspired by UML.
data.what_it_does: Implements type-safe hierarchical state machines using static blueprints and runtime instances. Supports advanced features like orthogonal regions, history semantics, pseudo-states, event deferral, and serialization.
use_when: You have complex state logic that suffers from state explosion in flat state machines
You need UML-compliant statecharts with hierarchy, concurrency, and history
avoid_when: You only need simple UI state holding or basic widget rebuilding
You prefer stream-based or simple bloc/cubit patterns for your application logic
strengths: Prevents state explosion with hierarchical parent/child states
Supports orthogonal regions, history semantics, and serialization
weaknesses: Steeper learning curve compared to standard state management packages
Requires careful definition of states, events, and transitions
